# Test fixtures

Everything here exists so the project can be developed and tested on a machine
with no Factorio installed.

## frames/

Five exported frames in this project's frame format, showing a factory growing
from 240 to 22,971 entities across 58 distinct entity types. Captured from a
real 100 hour Space Age save, converted to the frame schema, resource entities
removed, and cropped to expanding square regions around the busiest part of the
base.

Use these to build and test the renderer. They are real placements, so belt
runs, rail curves and mixed entity densities all look like a genuine factory
rather than synthetic noise.

    frame_0000.stfr     240 entities    3.7 KiB
    frame_0001.stfr     589 entities    8.6 KiB
    frame_0002.stfr   3,043 entities     42 KiB
    frame_0003.stfr  10,234 entities    141 KiB
    frame_0004.stfr  22,971 entities    315 KiB

## real-mod-settings.dat

A `mod-settings.dat` written by Factorio 2.0.77, holding 179 settings across
startup, runtime-global and runtime-per-user, from an install with roughly 30
mods.

This matters because it is genuine Factorio output. A fixture generated by our
own encoder would only prove the encoder agrees with itself. Round-tripping this
file byte for byte is what demonstrates the codec matches the real format,
including the empty-string encoding and the 64 bit integer types.

Note: this came from a real Factorio install, so it reveals which mods that
player had. Replace it with your own if you would rather not publish that. Any
`mod-settings.dat` from a 2.0 install works.

## fake-factorio

Not a file here, but the other half of developing without the game. It is a
binary in this crate that implements enough of Factorio's command line to
exercise the exporter:

    cargo run --bin fake-factorio -- --version
    cargo run --bin fake-factorio -- --benchmark save.zip --config c.ini --mod-directory mods/

Under `--benchmark` it reads `write-data` from the config file, decodes the
staged `mod-settings.dat`, and emits a frame only when the export trigger is
actually set. So a test using it verifies that settings staging really worked
instead of assuming it did.

Two knobs:

- `FAKE_FACTORIO_FRAME=<path>` emits that file as the frame instead of the
  built in one. Point it at `frames/frame_0003.stfr` for realistic volume.
- A save named `*-silent.zip` makes it exit cleanly having written nothing,
  reproducing the failure where the game runs fine but the mod never fires.

To run the real CLI against it, build a fake install tree with the binary at
`bin/x64/factorio` and an empty `data/` beside it, then pass `--factorio`.
